headline: US-Iran deal: $300bn private fund to trigger investment in Tehran
summary: More than half of the $300 billion fund has already been committed by global companies to encourage a final agreement between Washington and Tehran.
details: A $300 billion private investment fund, known as the Reconstruction and Development Fund, is outlined in a US-Iran framework agreement to incentivize a final deal.
More than half of this sum has already been committed by companies from the US, Gulf Arab states, Asia, South America, and Africa, according to a source with direct knowledge of the deal.
The fund is a private vehicle and will not include government grants or money, focusing on sectors like energy, logistics, manufacturing, and transport.
The agreement aims to end the conflict that began on February 28, halt the US blockade of Iran, and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a critical global oil and gas route.
Tehran had originally sought $400 billion in war damages from the US, but Washington declined, leading to the creation of this private investment fund instead.
The fund will only become operational once a final deal is signed. A 60-day memorandum of understanding will allow administrators to plan projects with Iranian officials and investors.
Access to the fund is contingent on Iran dismantling its nuclear programme, eliminating enriched material stockpiles, and accepting strict inspection regimes, as stated by Vice President JD Vance.
This financial mechanism is entirely separate from negotiations regarding the lifting of US sanctions and the release of frozen Iranian sovereign assets abroad.
caption:
A $300 billion private fund is being set up to trigger investment into Iran as part of a US-Iran framework agreement.

A $300 billion private investment fund, known as the Reconstruction and Development Fund, is outlined in a US-Iran framework agreement to incentivize a final deal.

More than half of this sum has already been committed by companies from the US, Gulf Arab states, Asia, South America, and Africa, according to a source with direct knowledge of the deal.

The fund is a private vehicle and will not include government grants or money, focusing on sectors like energy, logistics, manufacturing, and transport.

The agreement aims to end the conflict that began on February 28, halt the US blockade of Iran, and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a critical global oil and gas route.

Tehran had originally sought $400 billion in war damages from the US, but Washington declined, leading to the creation of this private investment fund instead.

The fund will only become operational once a final deal is signed. A 60-day memorandum of understanding will allow administrators to plan projects with Iranian officials and investors.

Access to the fund is contingent on Iran dismantling its nuclear programme, eliminating enriched material stockpiles, and accepting strict inspection regimes, as stated by Vice President JD Vance.

This financial mechanism is entirely separate from negotiations regarding the lifting of US sanctions and the release of frozen Iranian sovereign assets abroad.

headline: Shibir leader Jisan sent to jail in rape and forced abortion case
summary: A court in Comilla has ordered the central leader of Islami Chhatra Shibir to be sent to prison after denying him bail.
details: Jisan Mia Pradhan, a central leader of Islami Chhatra Shibir, has been sent to jail by a court in Comilla following allegations of rape and forced abortion.
